etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English welteren, equivalent to welt +‎ -er (frequentative suffix). Cognates include German Low German weltern (“to wallow; roll”), Old Norse velta (Danish vælte), German wälzen, Gothic 𐍅𐌰𐌻𐍄𐌾𐌰𐌽 (waltjan). Akin to wallow and Latin volvō.
senses: A general confusion or muddle, especially of a large number of items.
